routes.service: Best balance: huge winter, Tahoe access and a true one-seat train.

beaches.name: Pacific Grove / New Monterey border
beaches.gym: Sanctuary in Seaside has bouldering; truly late hours are the peninsula's weak point
beaches.fog: Frequent marine layer, especially late spring and summer
beaches.surf: Asilomar and outer-coast options; surfing is secondary here
beaches.strength: Best balanced daily system: bikeable shoreline, multiple coast orientations, San Carlos as the low-friction training fallback, an 18-mile coastal run/bike spine, and Carmel/Point Lobos about 15–20 minutes away.
beaches.conditions: Check live county bacterial advisories and post-rain conditions; rotate sites. Tourist traffic peaks near Cannery Row; the coastal core has less wildfire exposure than wooded inland edges.
beaches.directions: N Monterey Bay/Santa Cruz · S Carmel/Big Sur · E Fort Ord/Pinnacles · W Asilomar, tide pools and open Pacific

beaches.name: Santa Cruz / Capitola
beaches.gym: Pacific Edge offers bouldering and stays open to 10 p.m. on weekdays; Castle Rock adds outdoor bouldering
beaches.fog: Generally the sunnier finalist, though marine layer still occurs
beaches.surf: Best everyday surf variety in the five
beaches.strength: Narrowly beats Carmel under exact equal-thirds weighting: best land-life package, redwoods, mountain biking, outdoor bouldering, metro access and late-hours climbing; underwater clarity and depth are less consistently exceptional.
beaches.conditions: More urban activity and Highway 1 congestion; Santa Cruz Mountains add wildfire and smoke exposure.
beaches.directions: N redwoods/Half Moon Bay · S Monterey Peninsula · E Santa Cruz Mountains/Castle Rock · W surf, cliffs and Monterey Bay

beaches.name: Carmel-by-the-Sea
beaches.focus: Carmel Beach · Stillwater Cove · Point Lobos
beaches.gym: Sanctuary in Seaside is roughly 20–25 minutes; late-night climbing is weak
beaches.fog: Foggy periods, but somewhat more sun than the north side of the peninsula
beaches.surf: Beautiful white-sand beach; exposed conditions vary
beaches.strength: Highest underwater and shoreline-beauty ceiling. It loses the overall crown because Point Lobos diving is reservation-controlled, several premier areas are no-take, and the everyday run/bike network is less seamless.
beaches.conditions: Quiet and picturesque; visitor traffic and Highway 1 bottlenecks; wildfire exposure rises toward wooded hills and Big Sur.
beaches.directions: N Pacific Grove/Monterey · S Point Lobos/Big Sur · E Carmel Valley/Pinnacles · W white sand, canyon and open Pacific
